findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were mouse droppings observed to be in the dry storage area behind the shelving. The PIC stated that maintenance is in charge of cleaning. There were multiple mouse traps observed throughout this dry storage area and in other areas in the kitchen. A follow up is scheduled for 9/24/2026 to ensure that the mouse droppings have been cleaned up. Ensure that mouse droppings are being regularly cleaned up to allow for proper monitoring of rodent presence.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed mice droppings on the floor in the storage area behind the shelves. Person-in-charge (PIC) stated the facility was deep cleaned recently, however there were still traces of mice droppings. The inspectors instructed the PIC to contact their pest control operatives for mice inspection and also clean the mice droppings. Inspectors will be back in 2 weeks to spot check for mice droppings. Ensure the facility is free of pests and their droppings.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed light to be passing through the lower part of the back door. The PIC was informed to seal the opening. Ensure light from outside do not pass through doors or other entrances in the facility to prevent potential entry of insects and rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The taco meat in the warmer was observed to only be holding at 131F (probed). The PIC stated that the warmer was turned down lower than it should be at due to them not wanting the plastic of the cups to melt. CORRECTED- The PIC reheated the taco meat to 165F and turned the warmer up to hold at 135F and above. Ensure that hot food is holding at 135F and above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.
